newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ex-Amsterdam to North America booming, LatAm stead.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Amsterdam to North America booming, LatAm stead.

text.p: Despite expecting a slight downturn in June, those in the air cargo market have been slightly surprised to see business remaining strong to both North America and Latin America, a Reuters survey showed.

Jos van der Woensel, managing director of Zygene, a leading Dutch general sales agent, summed up the views of many when he said: "We do not know whether we are coming or going sometimes. January was incredibly busy and March was tremendous and business in May and June has not shown many signs of slowing down."
He, like most people, was expecting a slight drop-off in traffic in June. However, he stated: "There is only one word to describe capacity - full."

Van der Woensel added that a major stimulus for the steady growth is the perishables industry to North America. Many carriers are busy exporting Dutch-grown peppers, cucumbers and tomatoes to North America.
New markets in the North America have been opened up, he added, especially in Atlanta and the South U.S.

Destinations to Atlanta had seen considerable growth, he said, whereas destinations such as New York are more steady. Delta Airlines and KLM Royal Dutch Air lines are the only carriers with direct services to Atlanta.

Vegetable growers had perhaps opened up more markets themselves in the U.S. but also last year there was a large perishables exhibition held in Atlanta and this could have provided a boost for the south of the U.S., said Van der Woensel.
Even though perishables are the major stimulus currently, general cargo is also growing steadily, he added.
Dan de Wit, Speed managing director, told Reuters said cargo to destinations such as San Francisco, Los Angeles is very buoyant.
Speed bought Dutch carrier Martinair's belly capacity to those destinations as well as Toronto and has sold the space on an exclusive basis from April 7.
Martinair serves these destinations twice weekly, with the exception of Los Angeles which is three times weekly.
Toronto is operated with a B767, while the other two destinations are operated with an MD-11. The summer season operates from April until October.

Perishables traffic is very active to the North American destinations and accounts for roughly 40 percent of cargo there, said De Wit. The company is managing to send between 13 to 15 tonnes on each flight, he added.
Perishables traffic is not so strong to Toronto but general cargo is strong to that destination, he said. "We are certainly not complaining," he said.
VIA, general sales agent for Air Canada, Fred Veenendaal, was equally optimistic on prospects for the North American market in June.

"The market is booming," he said. May has been very busy and June is not slowing down, said Veenendaal. The west coast of the U.S. is especially buoyant to San Francisco, Seattle and Los Angeles. VIA trucks cargo to Paris and London for Air Canada's flights. Everything from chewing gum, vegetables or spare parts are going to North America, he added.

Rates to Canada and the U.S. are also appearing stable and slightly up in some cases such as Chicago and Miami. It is widely acknowledged that the carriers have not dropped the rates since the fuel surcharge ended. Most carriers absorbed the charge into their rates structure, thereby maintaining the healthier rates.
New York and Los Angeles remained the same at 1.80 guilders per kg and 2.45 guilders per kg respectively.
And there is a feeling that rates will be increasing in September/October time.
Carlo de Haas of general sales agent Air Support, said that North American traffic is doing very well.

One of the companies Air Support represents, Uzbekistan Airways increased capacity on its twice weekly New York flights by introducing a Boeing 767-300ER in early June, instead of an A310. These flights to New York have been very successful, he said, with flower exports making up most of the traffic to the U.S.
The service operates Tashkent-Amsterdam-New York.
Flowers are major shipments going to New York and to Uzbekistan,he said.

Rates to New York are perhaps those that have seen one of the largest changes over the last six months. They have firmed up and appear to be holding. Last year, rates to New York were below one guilder per kilogram to as low as 90 cents, said several industry sources.
MSAS' trade director Mischa de Boer said June has so-far, been fairly busy, with space hard to find both to east and west coast U.S. destinations.
Houston appears to be very strong at the moment, he added, especially for general cargo.
Latin America is steady but does not seem to be as buoyant as the North American market.
De Haas said there is undoubtedly more confidence in Miami as a transit point to Latin American destinations and more interest generally in many destinations there.
MSAS' De Boer said the forwarder is trying to increase its presence in the region as there is increasing economic growth there and more interest in the region.
MSAS has entered into a joint venture in Mexico and is currently in talks with agents in other parts of Latin America.

Zygene's Van der Woensel said that Latin America is stronger than in recent months, with Chile being the star destination. Zygene represents LanChile and he commented that flights are full to Chile, despite an expected drop in June.
"The Chilean market is booming, as the Chile becomes a stronger economic power."
Argentina seems to be at a bit of a standstill again and Colombia appears to be more variable.
Machinery, spare parts and electronics are the major exports from the Netherlands and vegetables, flowers and fish are imports from Latin America.

Rates in the Latin American market are mixed. Mexico is showing signs of being on the increase, when it went up slightly from 3.30 guilders per kg to 3.35 guilders. Chile also increased from 5.35 guilders to 5.45. But Bogota fell from 3.90 guilders to 3.80.
Several companies mentioned an excess capacity to South Africa and that the African market generally is fairly quiet.

Van der Woensel said Air Gabon is attracting more traffic from Europe and it has expanded its services within Africa. At the moment the airline has 83 percent schedule reliability, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
